full_name: Stochastic Accelerated Primal-Dual Method for Stochastic Bilinear Saddle-Point Problems
source_reference: Lan, First-order and Stochastic Optimization Methods for Machine Learning, Springer 2020, Section 4.4.2, Algorithm 4.3, Theorem 4.8, Corollary 4.3

problem.description: Stochastic bilinear saddle-point problem with smooth primal

variable_space.math: X \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n, \; Y \subseteq \mathbb{R}^m \text{ are closed convex sets equipped with inner products and norms}; \; A \text{ is a linear operator}

assumptions.name: Smoothness of hat_f
assumptions.math: \hat{f}(u) - \hat{f}(x) - \langle \nabla \hat{f}(x), u - x \rangle \le \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2} \|u - x\|^2, \quad \forall x, u \in X

assumptions.name: Simple convex function hat_g
assumptions.math: \hat{g} : Y \to \mathbb{R} \text{ is a relatively simple, proper, convex, lower semi-continuous function}

assumptions.name: Bregman divergences
assumptions.math:
V_X(x, u) := 
u_X(x) -

u_X(u), x - u angle, \quad V_Y(y, v) :=

u_X, 
u_Y 	ext{ are strongly convex functions with modulus } 1

assumptions.name: Stochastic first-order oracle and iid samples
assumptions.math: \text{At the } i\text{-th SFO call, input } (x_i,y_i) \in X \times Y \text{ produces } (\hat{G}(x_i),\hat{A}_x(x_i),\hat{A}_y(y_i)) := (G(x_i,\xi_i), A_x(x_i,\xi_i), A_y(y_i,\xi_i)), \text{ where } \{\xi_i\}_{i\ge 1} \text{ is i.i.d.}
assumptions.ref: Eq. (4.4.6) and the paragraph after it

assumptions.name: Assumption 8 (Bounded variance)
assumptions.math: \mathbb{E}[\|\hat{G}(x_i) - \nabla \hat{f}(x_i)\|_*^2] \le \sigma_{x,\hat{f}}^2, \quad \mathbb{E}[\|\hat{A}_x(x_i) - Ax_i\|_*^2] \le \sigma_y^2, \quad \mathbb{E}[\|\hat{A}_y(y_i) - A^T y_i\|_*^2] \le \sigma_{x,A}^2, \quad \forall x_i \in X,\; y_i \in Y

assumptions.name: Bounded domain (for Theorem 4.8)
assumptions.math: \sup_{x_1, x_2 \in X} V_X(x_1, x_2) \le D_X^2, \quad \sup_{y_1, y_2 \in Y} V_Y(y_1, y_2) \le D_Y^2

initialization.math: x_1 \in X, \; y_1 \in Y. \; \text{Set } \bar{x}_1 = x_1, \; \bar{y}_1 = y_1, \; \tilde{x}_1 = x_1

steps.name: Primal proximal update
steps.math: x_{t+1} = \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in X} \left\{ \langle \hat{G}(x_t), x \rangle + \langle x, \hat{A}_y(y_{t+1}) \rangle + \frac{1}{\eta_t} V_X(x, x_t) \right\}

conditions: \text{For all } t\ge 1, \beta_t,\theta_t,\eta_t,\tau_t \text{ in Algorithm 4.3 satisfy (4.4.24), (4.4.25), and (4.4.58) for some } p,q\in(0,1)
main_theorem.statement_math: \text{(a) Under Assumption 8, for all } t \ge 1, \quad \mathbb{E}[g(\bar{z}_{t+1})] \le Q_0(t), \quad \text{where } Q_0(t) := \frac{1}{\beta_t \gamma_t} \left\{ \frac{4\gamma_t}{\eta_t} D_X^2 + \frac{4\gamma_t}{\tau_t} D_Y^2 \right\} + \frac{1}{2\beta_t \gamma_t} \sum_{i=1}^{t} \left\{ \frac{(2-q)\eta_i \gamma_i}{1-q} \sigma_x^2 + \frac{(2-p)\tau_i \gamma_i}{1-p} \sigma_y^2 \right\}. \quad \text{(b) Under Assumption 9, for all } \lambda > 0 \text{ and } t \ge 1, \quad \mathrm{Prob}\{g(\bar{z}_{t+1}) > Q_0(t) + \lambda Q_1(t)\} \le 3\exp\{-\lambda^2/3\} + 3\exp\{-\lambda\}, \quad \text{where } Q_1(t) := \frac{1}{\beta_t \gamma_t} \left( 2\sigma_x D_X + \sqrt{2}\sigma_y D_Y \right) \sqrt{2\sum_{i=1}^{t} \gamma_i^2} + \frac{1}{2\beta_t \gamma_t} \sum_{i=1}^{t} \left\{ \frac{(2-q)\eta_i \gamma_i}{1-q} \sigma_x^2 + \frac{(2-p)\tau_i \gamma_i}{1-p} \sigma_y^2 \right\}.
main_theorem.rate: Theorem 4.8 gives the Q_0(t) and Q_1(t) bounds above. The simplified big-O rate is obtained only after the specific parameter choice in Corollary 4.3.

corollary_4_3.statement_math: \text{With the parameter choice (4.4.76), under Assumption 8, } Q_0(t) \le \frac{12L_{\hat f}D_X^2}{t(t+1)} + \frac{12\|A\|D_XD_Y}{t} + \frac{6\sqrt{2}(\sigma_xD_X+\sigma_yD_Y)}{\sqrt{t}}. \text{ If Assumption 9 also holds, } Q_1(t) \le \frac{5\sqrt{2}\sigma_xD_X + 4\sqrt{2}\sigma_yD_Y}{\sqrt{t}}.

main_theorem.measure: saddle gap g(\bar{z}_{t+1}) in expectation, and with high probability under Assumption 9

proof.description: Apply Proposition 4.12 to obtain the deterministic one-step recursion for beta_t Q(bar_z_{t+1}, z) - (beta_t - 1) Q(bar_z_t, z)
proof.math: \beta_t Q(\bar{z}_{t+1}, z) - (\beta_t - 1)Q(\bar{z}_t, z) \le \langle \nabla \hat{f}(x_t^{md}), x_{t+1} - x \rangle + \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_t} \|x_{t+1} - x_t\|^2 + [\hat{g}(y_{t+1}) - \hat{g}(y)] + \langle Ax_{t+1}, y \rangle - \langle Ax, y_{t+1} \rangle

proof.description: Substitute the optimality conditions of the stochastic prox updates (4.4.56)--(4.4.57) into Proposition 4.12, isolate noise terms Delta^i, and telescope using Lemma 4.9
proof.math: \beta_t \gamma_t Q(\bar{z}_{t+1}, z) \le B_t(z, z_{[t]}) + \gamma_t \langle A(x_{t+1} - x_t), y - y_{t+1} \rangle - \gamma_t \left(\frac{q}{2\eta_t} - \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_t}\right) \|x_{t+1} - x_t\|^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{t} \Lambda_i(z)

proof.description: Control the stochastic error sum via the auxiliary prox sequence from Lemma 4.10

Take expectations: \mathbb{E}[\langle \Delta^i, z_i^v - z_i angle] = 0 by the martingale property, \mathbb{E}[\|\Delta_x^i\|_*^2] \le \sigma_x^2, \mathbb{E}[\|\Delta_y^i\|_*^2] \le \sigma_y^2; use the B_t bounds with D_X^2 and D_Y^2
For the high-probability bound (part b), apply Lemma 4.1 to the martingale-difference terms and Markov's inequality to the quadratic noise terms under Assumption 9

source_scope_notes: Theorem 4.8 itself is recorded only as the Q_0(t)/Q_1(t) bounds under (4.4.34), (4.4.24), (4.4.25), (4.4.58), and Assumptions 8/9 as stated above.
The simplified big-O rate is recorded under Corollary 4.3, not as an unconditional part of Theorem 4.8.
No Lean-only measurability, integrability, or selector-existence obligations are added as source assumptions in this JSON.

Eq. (4.4.57) uses \hat{G}(x_t), while the following noise definition compares it to \nabla\hat{f}(x_t^{md}); this JSON keeps that source notation and does not silently replace \hat{G}(x_t) by \hat{G}(x_t^{md}).

Eq. (4.4.6) states SFO inputs in X \times Y, while Algorithm 4.3 calls \hat{A}_x(\tilde{x}_t); this JSON records the book's statements as written and does not add an extra hypothesis such as \tilde{x}_t \in X or an ambient oracle-domain assumption.

key_lemmas.name: Three-point lemma (Lemma 3.5)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{If } \hat{u} \in \operatorname{Argmin}\{p(u) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, u) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, u) : u \in X\}, \text{ then } \forall u \in X: \quad p(\hat{u}) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, \hat{u}) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, \hat{u}) \le p(u) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, u) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, u) - (\mu_1 + \mu_2) V(\hat{u}, u)
key_lemmas.role: Provides the per-step prox inequality used in deriving the optimality conditions for both primal and dual updates

proof.description: Write the first-order optimality condition of the minimization defining hat_u
Use the Bregman three-point identity to rewrite the linear terms and obtain the decrease inequality
proof.math: p(\hat{u}) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, \hat{u}) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, \hat{u}) \le p(u) + \mu_1 V(\tilde{x}, u) + \mu_2 V(\tilde{y}, u) - (\mu_1 + \mu_2) V(\hat{u}, u)

key_lemmas.name: Mirror-descent summation lemma (Lemma 4.3)
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let } \zeta_1, \ldots, \zeta_j \text{ be a sequence of elements of } \mathbb{R}^n. \text{ Define } v_{t+1} = \operatorname{argmin}_{x \in X}\{\langle \zeta_t, x \rangle + V(v_t, x)\}. \text{ Then for any } x \in X, \quad \langle \zeta_t, v_t - x \rangle \le V(v_t, x) - V(v_{t+1}, x) + \frac{\|\zeta_t\|_*^2}{2}, \quad \sum_{t=1}^{j} \langle \zeta_t, v_t - x \rangle \le V(v_1, x) + \frac{1}{2} \sum_{t=1}^{j} \|\zeta_t\|_*^2
key_lemmas.role: Provides the one-step mirror-descent bound used inside the auxiliary prox sequence of Lemma 4.10

proof.description: Apply the prox three-point inequality to the update defining v_{t+1}
proof.math: \langle \zeta_t, v_t - x \rangle \le V(v_t, x) - V(v_{t+1}, x) + \langle \zeta_t, v_t - v_{t+1} \rangle - V(v_t, v_{t+1})

proof.description: Bound the residual by Cauchy-Schwarz and strong convexity of the distance generating function

key_lemmas.name: Proposition 4.12
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{If } \bar{z}_{t+1} = (\bar{x}_{t+1}, \bar{y}_{t+1}) \text{ is generated by Algorithm 4.2 with } \beta_t \ge 1, \text{ then } \forall z = (x,y) \in Z: \quad \beta_t Q(\bar{z}_{t+1}, z) - (\beta_t - 1) Q(\bar{z}_t, z) \le \langle \nabla \hat{f}(x_t^{md}), x_{t+1} - x \rangle + \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_t} \|x_{t+1} - x_t\|^2 + [\hat{g}(y_{t+1}) - \hat{g}(y)] + \langle Ax_{t+1}, y \rangle - \langle Ax, y_{t+1} \rangle
key_lemmas.role: Provides the deterministic one-step saddle-gap recursion that forms the basis for the stochastic analysis

proof.description: Use convexity of hat_f and the aggregate update to bound beta_t hat_f(bar_x_{t+1}) - (beta_t - 1) hat_f(bar_x_t)
Use convexity of hat_g and the aggregate y-update to handle the dual term
Combine with the definition of Q in Eq. (4.4.20) and the bilinear coupling term
proof.math: \beta_t Q(\bar{z}_{t+1}, z) - (\beta_t - 1) Q(\bar{z}_t, z) \le \langle \nabla \hat{f}(x_t^{md}), x_{t+1} - x \rangle + \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_t} \|x_{t+1} - x_t\|^2 + [\hat{g}(y_{t+1}) - \hat{g}(y)] + \langle Ax_{t+1}, y \rangle - \langle Ax, y_{t+1} \rangle

key_lemmas.name: Lemma 4.9
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Assume the parameters } \beta_t, \theta_t, \eta_t, \tau_t \text{ satisfy (4.4.24), (4.4.25), and } \frac{q}{\eta_t} - \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{\beta_t} - \frac{\|A\|^2 \tau_t}{p} \ge 0 \text{ for some } p,q\in(0,1). \text{ Then } \forall z \in Z: \quad \beta_t \gamma_t Q(\bar{z}_{t+1}, z) \le B_t(z, z_{[t]}) + \gamma_t \langle A(x_{t+1} - x_t), y - y_{t+1} \rangle - \gamma_t \left(\frac{q}{2\eta_t} - \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_t}\right) \|x_{t+1} - x_t\|^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{t} \Lambda_i(z), \quad \Lambda_i(z) := - \frac{(1-q)\gamma_i}{2\eta_i} \|x_{i+1} - x_i\|^2 - \frac{(1-p)\gamma_i}{2\tau_i} \|y_{i+1} - y_i\|^2 - \gamma_i \langle \Delta^i, z_{i+1} - z \rangle
key_lemmas.role: Lifts the deterministic APD recursion to the stochastic setting by isolating the noise in Lambda_i(z)

proof.description: Write the optimality conditions of the stochastic prox updates (4.4.56)--(4.4.57) and substitute into Proposition 4.12
proof.math: \beta_t \gamma_t Q(\bar{z}_{t+1}, z) - (\beta_t - 1) \gamma_t Q(\bar{z}_t, z) \le \frac{\gamma_t}{\eta_t} V_X(x, x_t) - \frac{\gamma_t}{\eta_t} V_X(x, x_{t+1}) + \frac{\gamma_t}{\tau_t} V_Y(y, y_t) - \frac{\gamma_t}{\tau_t} V_Y(y, y_{t+1}) + \gamma_t \langle A(x_{t+1} - x_t), y - y_{t+1} \rangle - \gamma_{t-1} \langle A(x_t - x_{t-1}), y - y_t \rangle - \gamma_t \left(\frac{1}{2\eta_t} - \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_t}\right) \|x_{t+1} - x_t\|^2 - \frac{\gamma_t}{2\tau_t} \|y_{t+1} - y_t\|^2 - \gamma_{t-1} \langle A(x_t - x_{t-1}), y_t - y_{t+1} \rangle - \gamma_t \langle \Delta_{x,t}^{\hat{f}} + \Delta_{x,t}^A, x_{t+1} - x \rangle - \gamma_t \langle \Delta_t^y, y_{t+1} - y \rangle

proof.description: Bound the coupling term by Cauchy-Schwarz/Young using Eq. (4.4.25) and telescope inductively
proof.math: (\beta_{t+1} - 1)\gamma_{t+1} Q(\bar{z}_{t+1}, z) - (\beta_1 - 1)\gamma_1 Q(\bar{z}_1, z) \le B_t(z, z_{[t]}) + \gamma_t \langle A(x_{t+1} - x_t), y - y_{t+1} \rangle - \gamma_t \left(\frac{q}{2\eta_t} - \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_t}\right) \|x_{t+1} - x_t\|^2 - \sum_{i=1}^{t-1} \gamma_i \left(\frac{q}{2\eta_i} - \frac{L_{\hat{f}}}{2\beta_i} - \frac{\|A\|^2 \tau_i}{2p}\right) \|x_{i+1} - x_i\|^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{t} \Lambda_i(z)

key_lemmas.name: Lemma 4.10
key_lemmas.statement_math: \text{Let } \eta_i, \tau_i \text{ and } \gamma_i, \; i = 1, 2, \ldots, \text{ be given positive constants. For any } z_1 \in Z, \text{ if we define } z_1^v = z_1 \text{ and } z_{i+1}^v = \operatorname{argmin}_{z=(x,y) \in Z} \{-\eta_i \langle \Delta_x^i, x \rangle - \tau_i \langle \Delta_y^i, y \rangle + V(z, z_i^v)\}, \text{ then } \sum_{i=1}^{t} \gamma_i \langle -\Delta^i, z_i^v - z \rangle \le B_t(z, z_{[t]}^v) + \sum_{i=1}^{t} \frac{\eta_i \gamma_i}{2} \|\Delta_x^i\|_*^2 + \sum_{i=1}^{t} \frac{\tau_i \gamma_i}{2} \|\Delta_y^i\|_*^2
key_lemmas.role: Constructs an auxiliary prox process that absorbs the martingale noise terms in sum_i Lambda_i(z)

proof.description: Split the prox update into separate x- and y-components and apply Lemma 4.3 to each block
proof.math: V_X(x, x_{i+1}^v) \le V_X(x, x_i^v) - \eta_i \langle \Delta_x^i, x - x_i^v \rangle + \frac{\eta_i^2 \|\Delta_x^i\|_*^2}{2}

proof.description: Multiply by gamma_i and sum over i to telescope the Bregman divergences

key_lemmas.name: Lemma 4.1
key_lemmas.role: Provides the large-deviation bound for martingale-difference sums used in the high-probability part of Theorem 4.8

proof.description: Control the conditional exponential moment and apply the exponential-supermartingale argument
